jp: 夕食[ゆうしょく]を{作[つく]りかけた|cv-kakeru}とき、卵[たまご]がないことに気[き]づいて、スーパーへ走[はし]った。
en: When I had started making dinner, I noticed there were no eggs and ran to the supermarket.
why: 〜かける means 'be in the middle of / have just begun', so 作りかけた fits stopping partway to shop.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]の野菜[やさい]が{腐[くさ]りかけて|cv-kakeru}いたので、急[いそ]いで食[た]べた。
en: The vegetables in the fridge were about to go bad, so I ate them quickly.
why: 腐りかける means 'on the verge of rotting'; completely rotten vegetables would not be eaten.

jp: 気[き]に入[い]ったセーターを{買[か]いかけた|cv-kakeru}が、値札[ねふだ]を見[み]てやめた。
en: I was about to buy a sweater I liked, but I saw the price tag and stopped.
why: 買いかけた is 'started to buy but did not finish', which matches stopping at the price tag.

jp: 友[とも]だちに「ランチ代[だい]は割[わ]り勘[かん]にしよう」と{持[も]ちかけました|cv-kakeru}。
en: I proposed to my friend that we split the lunch bill.
why: 持ちかける means to approach someone with a proposal; the other verbs are about carrying things.

jp: 市場[いちば]のおじさんは、買[か]い物客[ものきゃく]一人[ひとり]一人[ひとり]に笑顔[えがお]で{語[かた]りかけて|cv-kakeru}いた。
en: The man at the market was speaking warmly to each shopper with a smile.
why: 語りかける is to address someone directly, a one-way action towards each customer.

jp: {使[つか]いかけの|cv-kakeru}洗剤[せんざい]がまだ残[のこ]っているのに、新[あたら]しいのを買[か]ってしまった。
en: I bought a new bottle even though I still had a half-used bottle of detergent.
why: 使いかけの means 'partly used'; a bottle that is used up (切った, 果たした) could not still be left.

jp: レジで、おつりを渡[わた]し忘[わす]れた店員[てんいん]が、店[みせ]を出[で]たお客[きゃく]さんを{追[お]いかけて|cv-kakeru}いった。
en: The clerk who had forgotten to hand over the change ran after the customer who had left the shop.
why: 追いかける is to chase after someone to catch them; the others mean driving someone away.

jp: 近所[きんじょ]のパン屋[や]に{行[い]きかけた|cv-kakeru}が、定休日[ていきゅうび]だと思[おも]い出[だ]してやめた。
en: I was about to go to the bakery nearby, but I remembered it was closed that day and gave up.
why: 行きかける means to set out but not complete the trip, which fits giving up halfway.

jp: アイスクリームが{溶[と]けかけて|cv-kakeru}いたので、すぐ冷凍庫[れいとうこ]に戻[もど]した。
en: The ice cream had started to melt, so I put it straight back in the freezer.
why: 溶けかける means 'beginning to melt', the reason to return it to the freezer.

jp: レジで財布[さいふ]から千円札[せんえんさつ]を{出[だ]しかけた|cv-kakeru}とき、カードが使[つか]えると言[い]われた。
en: I had just started taking a thousand-yen note out of my wallet at the register when I was told I could use a card.
why: 出しかけた means the action was begun but interrupted, which the clerk's remark explains.

jp: 買[か]ってきた材料[ざいりょう]で、さっそくカレー作[づく]りに{取[と]りかかった|cv-kakeru}。
en: With the ingredients I had bought, I immediately set about making curry.
why: 〜に取りかかる means to start work on a task; the other 取り〜 verbs take an object with を, not a task with に.
